post.title: First snow, clear water
post.body:
The first snow of the season came down to the lake over the weekend, so on a sunny, cold morning Marley and I drove up into the mountains to see the snow and fly the drone. First we stopped at Spooner Lake so Marley could play in the snow, then we headed for Chimney Beach on the east side of Lake Tahoe.

## Red coat, white path

At 8:37 at Spooner Lake she was standing in the middle of a snowy path in her red coat, with water showing through the trees behind her and one tree still holding its yellow leaves. A few minutes later I stopped for a quick selfie under the pines. The snow was patchy there, white in the open and gone wherever the needles were thick, and Marley was already off ahead, nose down. She also got her ball, and chased it across the slippery ice and snow.

## Up over Chimney Beach

Just after nine the drone was up over the shore. From up there the water does things you never see from the beach. Near the boulders it's pale turquoise, then green, then a deep blue where the bottom drops away. You can count the rocks on the lakebed. In a couple of shots the trees on the shore throw long shadows straight out across the bottom, like stripes.

> From up there the water does things you never see from the beach.

The snow had reached the shoreline too. Looking straight down at 9:09 and again at 9:17, there's a dusting of white between the granite and the trees, right at the edge of all that blue.

## Going wide

Then I turned the camera for the wide view. The forest runs down to the water in one long line, point after point, and the mountains across the lake already had snow on top. The sky was full of thin rippled cloud. At 9:19 I went straight down into the shallows again: stones scattered on pale sand, the water so clear it barely looks like water.

On the drive back down the mountain, Marley was one tired dog.

What I learned: the first snow and a clear, cold morning are worth the early drive. The same shoreline looks completely different from above, and a short flight that goes close, straight down, then wide gives you a whole story to work with.

episode.title: Snow on the shore
episode.script:
Narrated by Starlee.

It was the second of November, a little after half past eight, sunny and cold, and the first snow of the season had come all the way down to Lake Tahoe.

So Christian and Marley drove up into the mountains to see it. The plan was simple. First, a stop at Spooner Lake, so Marley could play in the snow. Then the drone, up over Chimney Beach, on the east side of the lake.

There wasn't much snow at Spooner. Just enough to turn a path white and show every footprint. Marley stood in the middle of it in her bright red coat. Behind her, through the trees, there was water. And off to one side, one stubborn tree was still holding on to its yellow leaves, as if nobody had told it what month it was.

A few minutes later, under the tall pines, Christian stopped for a selfie. A small, satisfied smile. In the background Marley had already moved on. Her nose was down, and her red coat was the brightest thing in the forest. And when the ball came out, she went after it across the slippery ice and snow.

***

Then, just after nine, the story changed altitude.

The drone went up over the shore at Chimney Beach. And this is where Christian's eye shows. He didn't settle for one pretty view. He went straight down over the boulders, where the water turns from pale turquoise to green to a deep, deep blue. He caught the rocks on the bottom, sharp enough to count. And he caught the morning shadows of the shoreline trees, stretched out across the lakebed like long dark stripes.

Look closely and the snow is there too. A fine white dusting sat between the granite and the pines, right at the edge of the water. That's the first snow, meeting a lake that still looked like summer.

***

Then he turned the camera outward. The forest ran down to the water in one long line, point after point. Far across the lake, the mountains already wore white caps. Thin rippled clouds filled the sky.

At nineteen past nine he went straight down again into the shallows. Scattered stones sat on pale sand, under water so clear it hardly looked like water at all.

He could have kept every shot. What he kept was a sequence. It starts close, goes straight down, then wide, and ends close again. Knowing how to put the pictures in order is half of telling a story.

On the drive back down the mountain, Marley was one tired dog.

Some mornings are about where you went. This one was about how you looked at it.

questions: Privacy: you said the drive started in Carson City. I kept the town out and wrote only that you drove up into the mountains, since naming where you set out could point toward home. OK to leave it that way?
The ball clips (clip-1 to clip-4) are stamped 11:01, after the flight, but the Spooner photos are 8:37 and 8:40. I placed the ball play at the Spooner stop before the flight. Is that right?
Photo 17 didn't come through for me, so its caption comes from your note (Marley tired on the drive back), without the word home. Does that match the picture?
